e.etymology: A modern blend of May with the -lin ending, used by both English- and Spanish-speaking American families. It can also render the Chinese name Mei-Lin.
A spelling of Christopher common among Spanish speakers, in line with Cristo and Cristóbal. Christopher is from Greek Khristophoros, bearing Christ.
From Latin iustus, just or fair. It was the name of several early saints and of three men in the New Testament, and it has long been used in Germany and the Netherlands.

The South Asian spelling of Arabic sayyid, lord or master, an honorific for descendants of the Prophet Muhammad. In Pakistan, India and Bangladesh it is often a family title placed before a personal name.

e.meaning: form of Jacob, traditionally read as supplanter
e.etymology: A K respelling of Jacoby, a surname derived from Jacob, the Hebrew patriarch's name traditionally read as heel-holder or supplanter. The ending echoes Kobe.
From County Tyrone in Northern Ireland, Irish Tír Eoghain, the land of Eoghan, once a Gaelic kingdom. Actor Tyrone Power, whose family was Irish, made it familiar in the US.
namesakes: Tyrone Power (film star of the 1930s to 1950s)
e.note: Often used in jokes and memes as a stock name for a Black man.

e.etymology: A short form of Louis, Louise and Louisa, which go back through French to the Frankish name Chlodovech, famous in battle. It is used on its own for both boys and girls.
namesakes: Lou Reed (Velvet Underground singer and songwriter)
e.note: Sounds the same as loo, British slang for a toilet.

e.etymology: A recent American coinage with no traditional meaning. The closest well-known bearer is NBA guard Jrue Holiday, whose name is pronounced like Drew.
The island of Arthurian legend where the wounded King Arthur was taken. Geoffrey of Monmouth's Latin Insula Avallonis is usually traced to a Celtic word for apple, as in Welsh afal.

assoc.t: Avalon, the enchanted island of Arthurian legend
Toyota Avalon, a full-size sedan sold until 2022
Avalon, resort town on Catalina Island, California
Avalon, Roxy Music's 1982 album and song

e.etymology: From Hebrew li, to me, and or, light, with the feminine ending -a: the feminine of Lior. It is a modern Israeli name, also spelled Leora.

e.meaning: pet form of Jack or Jacqueline
e.etymology: From Jack with the -ie ending. For boys it is a pet form of Jack and John; for girls it is short for Jacqueline, the French feminine of Jacques, a form of Jacob.
namesakes: Jackie Robinson (first Black player in modern Major League Baseball)

e.etymology: A French elaboration of Nadia, itself from Nadya, the Russian pet form of Nadezhda, hope. It is also a favorite in Lebanon and Germany.

assoc.t: Nadine, Chuck Berry's 1964 rock and roll hit

e.etymology: A Biblical name: Jahziel, also written Jahzeel, is a son of Naphtali in Genesis and 1 Chronicles. It is Hebrew, from a root meaning to divide or allot, joined with El, God.
An English surname of Norman origin, also spelled Tyrrell. It is usually traced to Old French tirer, to pull, as a nickname for a stubborn person. It became a US first name in the 20th century.
namesakes: Terrell Owens (Hall of Fame NFL wide receiver)
Terrell Davis (Hall of Fame Denver Broncos running back)

e.etymology: A shortened spelling of Isaiah, from Hebrew Yesha'yahu, the Lord is salvation, the name of the Old Testament prophet.
namesakes: Isiah Thomas (Hall of Fame Detroit Pistons guard)
Isiah Pacheco (Kansas City Chiefs running back)

assoc.t: Isiah Thomas, Hall of Fame Pistons point guard

e.etymology: From the Greek city of Larissa and the nymph of the same name; the place name is thought to mean citadel in a pre-Greek language. It spread through an early Orthodox martyr and Russian Larisa.

assoc.t: Larissa, city in Thessaly, central Greece

e.etymology: A modern fanciful spelling of Briley, an English surname taken up as a first name. Its sound sits between Bryce, Riley and the popular -leigh names.
A modern member of the Adaline and Adalyn family, which goes back to Germanic adal, noble. It can also be read as a spelling of the French name Adélie.
A spelling of Kian, which has two sources: Persian Kian, kings, the name of Iran's legendary Kayanian dynasty, and the Irish name Cian, ancient or enduring.
In Indian American families a short spelling of Niyam, from Sanskrit niyama, a rule or observance. Its sound is close to Liam and to the Irish girls' name Niamh, which is said NEEV.
A 20th-century coinage alongside Darian, possibly based on Darius or Dorian. The spelling matches the Darién region of Panama and the town of Darien, Connecticut.

assoc.t: Darien, affluent Connecticut suburb of New York
Darién Gap, jungle between Panama and Colombia

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that joins the Bray- of Brayden with the -lin ending of Jaylin and Kaylin. It is used for both boys and girls.
From Arabic rim, a white gazelle. The gazelle is a classic image of grace and beauty in Arabic poetry, which made the word a girls' name.
A spelling of Citlali, from Nahuatl citlalin, star. The X follows other Nahuatl names such as Xochitl, and the name is popular with Mexican American families.
From the Arabic root for friendliness and close companionship. It is best known from Anas ibn Malik, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad who passed on many hadith.
e.note: English speakers may misread it as close to the word anus; the Arabic pronunciation is nearer AH-nass.

e.etymology: A modern American name with no settled source. Its sound follows Biblical names such as Isaiah, Josiah and Azariah, with the Az- opening of Aziel and Azriel.
The English spelling of Spanish Inés and Portuguese Inês, forms of Agnes, from Greek hagne, pure or chaste. It entered English through 18th-century poems and plays about Inês de Castro.

e.meaning: air; a song for solo voice
e.etymology: A respelling of Aria, the Italian word for air that came to mean a solo song in opera. The y also recalls Arya, a Sanskrit name meaning noble and a Game of Thrones heroine.
Taken from the Black Sea port of Odessa in Ukraine, named in 1795 after the ancient Greek colony Odessos. As a girls' name it has also been linked with Odysseus and the Odyssey.

assoc.t: Odesa, Black Sea port city in Ukraine
Odessa, West Texas oil city of Friday Night Lights

e.etymology: The Spanish form of Ephraim, written Efraín in Spanish, from Hebrew Efrayim, fruitful. In Genesis, Ephraim is the younger son of Joseph and founder of one of the tribes of Israel.
The Hebrew word for lion. It has been a Jewish given name for centuries, often paired with Yiddish Leib and tied to the lion that stands for the tribe of Judah.
A respelling of Laken, a name that entered US use in the 1980s through the soap opera Santa Barbara. It is commonly heard as Lake with the -en ending of Lauren or Camryn.

assoc.t: Laken Riley, student whose 2024 killing led to a US law
